messages:
sam_customer: Hey @support — over the last 20m we started seeing 2–3s tails and intermittent 502/403s from our production route. The Console shows Region: eu-west-1 for the route, but our request logs show serving region as us-east-1. Can you check?

jess_support: Thanks Sam — can you paste one request-id and an example timestamp? Also which API endpoint/route are you hitting?

sam_customer: request id: req_01F8XYZ9Q0, occurred 2026-03-16 18:41:02 UTC. Endpoint: POST /v1/generate (project X, route default). I reproduced with curl: 

curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'

Response headers included: 
  x-rw-serving-region: us-east-1
  x-rw-request-id: req_01F8XYZ9Q0
  x-rw-latency-ms: 2187

But in the Console UI the route card says: Region: eu-west-1. Billing dashboard is also showing tokens on eu-west-1 which doesn't match the serving logs.

jess_support: Ack. I'm escalating to runtime and SRE. Adding @anita_runtime and @mike_sre.

anita_runtime: Thanks — quick context: we have routing policy that prefers the route's configured region but will fallback when capacity/tags don't match. Two things to check quickly: (1) whether the control-plane route metadata is out of sync on edge nodes, and (2) whether token scoping/tenant routing caused an auth fallback to a different tenant region. Can you run a quick check and include full raw request headers (minus the auth token)?

sam_customer: Pasted headers (sanitized): 
  Host: api.redwood.example
  Authorization: Bearer [redacted]
  Content-Type: application/json
  X-Client-Region: eu-west-1
  User-Agent: curl/7.88.1
  X-Request-ID: req_01F8XYZ9Q0

Also billing_ops: invoice for project X shows egress in us-east-1 for the same intervals. That explains unexpected network costs on our side.

mike_sre: Noted. I just checked control-plane sync metrics around 1867880000 UNIX ~ 20m ago — we had a failed write to the region-tagging service during a deploy (deploy id deploy-2026-03-16-18:28). That could leave the console metadata updated but the runtime routing table still referencing old tags.

anita_runtime: Repro steps I recommend for validation:
1) From your client, run: 
   curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" \
     -H "X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: eu-west-1" \
     -d '{"prompt":"ping"}'
2) Inspect response headers for x-rw-serving-region. If it is us-east-1 despite the Prefer header, runtime routing is ignoring route config.
3) On our side I ran: 
   curl -s https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routes/projectX/default | jq .region_tag
   (control plane returned: "eu-west-1")
   But router table on node edge-23: 
   ssh edge-23 -- sudo /usr/local/bin/routing-check --route default 
   output: serving_region=us-east-1, source=runtime-cache, last_sync=1867878000

So control plane shows eu-west-1, console reads eu-west-1 (console-bot synced), but edge node has cached us-east-1. Looks like cache didn't get the final sync after the tagging deploy.

jess_support: What's the quick mitigation? Customers are seeing errors and billing mismatch.

anita_runtime: Immediate mitigation: force config resync on affected edges and invalidate routing cache for projectX/default. Command for SRE: 

  sudo systemctl restart redwood-edge-sync && 
  /usr/local/bin/routing-invalidate --project projectX --route default

I'll prepare a hotfix so subsequent deploys include stronger write-retry for the tagging service.

mike_sre: I'll run the resync on edge-22..edge-26 now. Also checking for auth fallbacks: nothing in auth logs indicating tenant mismatch; token scopes look fine.

billing_ops: Heads up — if serving region changes, billing attribution may be corrected retrospectively once logs are reprocessed, but if traffic actually served in us-east-1 there may be genuine cross-region charges. We can open an invoice review after we confirm the timeframe.

anita_runtime: jess_support can you trigger the resync and ask customer to re-run the curl with the Prefer header?

jess_support: Doing the resync now.

console-bot: control-plane: region-tagging-service: deploy-2026-03-16-18:28 — recovered. Resync initiated for affected edges: edge-22..edge-26.

mike_sre: Resync completed on edge-22..edge-26. routing cache last_sync updated to 1867890300.

sam_customer: Re-ran test at 2026-03-16 18:40:45 UTC. New response headers: 
  x-rw-serving-region: eu-west-1
  x-rw-request-id: req_01F8XYZ9Z
  x-rw-latency-ms: 214

503/403s are gone and p95 latency back to ~220ms. Billing still shows some us-east-1 usage for the earlier window, will coordinate with billing_ops. Thanks everyone! :party-parrot:

jess_support: Great — marking as resolved for now. We'll follow up with a postmortem and patch to add retries and a control-plane write-ack check so console/runtime can't diverge in future.

mike_sre: I'll open an incident PR with notes and timeline, CC billing_ops for invoice review.

billing_ops: We'll contact you Sam if we need additional logs for adjustment.

sam_customer: Appreciate the fast triage.
